plan_a_advantages: More frequent easy runs promote consistent aerobic development.
The single longer run is appropriately scaled for the goal of endurance.
Lower overall volume reduces the risk of overtraining.
plan_b_advantages: Includes hill and tempo work, which are beneficial for trail running strength and speed.
The longer runs are more substantial in duration, providing a greater stimulus for endurance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent aerobic development with frequent easy runs and a single, longer run, which is crucial for building a solid endurance base. Plan B, while including some hill work and tempo runs, has a higher volume of harder sessions and less dedicated time for consistent aerobic work, potentially leading to overtraining and hindering speed development. Plan A’s focus on low-intensity, frequent running is more aligned with the goal of improving speed in trail running, as it allows for greater adaptation and recovery.
